provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1922 Tours Mame antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: Mame prints Alleluja / alleluja with j where the 1962 prints Alleluia / alleluia with i (four occurrences); no other letter differs.. Corroboration: 1862 Pustet page-image collation of 2026-08-26, Pustet printed p. [37]; Internet Archive leaf n706 (Pustet Alleluja uses j; target Alleluia uses i.), outcome collated-non-exact. The Pustet's single recorded non-exactness here is the j of Alleluja. THE MAME SHARES IT. The Mame is a French printing that uses j for consonantal i throughout its body text, so its j-forms here are systematic house orthography, not a local variant. On this point the Mame AGREES WITH THE 1862 PUSTET AGAINST THE 1962, so the human review's observation stands on two independent public-domain witnesses, and no public-domain page yet seen authorises the 1962's i-spelling of this word as an exact string..
